title: A persisted pid was checked against the wrong machine's process table

first_order.what_broke: Two places persist a pid and later ask `os.kill(pid, 0)` whether it is alive. Neither recorded which machine minted it. The queue lease minted owners as `pid:uuid`, so `run.py::_owner_is_gone` reclaimed a row held by a LIVE worker on another host and put two workers on one candidate — the double publish the lease exists to prevent. The consumer heartbeat wrote a bare `pid`, so `consumer.py::consumer_liveness` read a healthy remote consumer as `dead` and paged for it. Both were latent while everything ran on one laptop. The engine moved to Fly on 2026-08-18 and task #60 asks for more instances, so both were about to fire.
first_order.receipt: Reconstructed the pre-fix `_owner_is_gone` and ran it: a three-part owner parsed `host` as the pid, found it non-numeric and returned False, so the parse was never the bug — the MINT was, because the owner had no host to check. On the consumer side, three of the five new tests fail against the committed `consumer.py` and pass after the fix: test_every_beat_carries_the_host_that_minted_its_pid, test_a_consumer_on_another_machine_is_never_paged_as_dead, test_a_remote_consumer_that_really_died_is_still_caught_by_staleness.
first_order.fixed_by: prospector a6898c30 (the lease) and this commit (the heartbeat and the shared host id)

cause_chain: A pid was persisted as if it were a global identifier. It is not: it names a slot in ONE machine's process table.

The liveness rule was right and the input was wrong. `_owner_is_gone` and `_pid_alive` both already said 'unsure means alive' and both already had a way to express it. Neither could apply it, because nothing on the record said the pid was foreign.

The estate had no single definition of 'which machine am I', so each site would have grown its own. `claim_lock.py` already recorded `socket.gethostname()`; the lease and the heartbeat did not, and nothing compared them.
The assumption was true for as long as there was one machine, and nothing in the code recorded that it WAS an assumption. It became false on 2026-08-18 without a single line changing.

CLASS: an identifier that is only unique within a boundary must carry that boundary, or the first day the boundary moves, every check on it silently answers a different question. This is the same class as the store resolver that followed the CODE instead of the store (INC-2026-08-18-store-resolver): both are environment assumptions that no assertion ever stated.

second_order.sweep_command: rg -n 'os\.kill' -g '*.py' prospector/ scripts/ && rg -n 'getpid\(\)' -g '*.py' prospector/ scripts/
second_order.note: RUN 2026-08-19. Every `os.kill` on a pid that came from PERSISTED state: prospector/run.py (the lease, fixed a6898c30), prospector/consumer.py (the heartbeat, fixed here), and prospector/ops/runs.py::process_alive (the run records, NOT fixed here — see below). scripts/watch_engine.py and scripts/popdd_verify.py read a pid file written by a process on the same box in the same run, so they are same-machine by construction; prospector/ops/runner.py and the tests all kill a child they spawned themselves. prospector/claim_lock.py already records `host` beside its pid, which is what the others now do. THE FIRST SWEEP MISSED process_alive because its output was truncated with `head -20` — recorded here rather than quietly corrected, because a truncated sweep is the same defect class as the one being swept for.

third_order.mechanism: tests/unit/test_queue_lease.py (5 tests, of which test_every_lease_owner_carries_the_host_that_minted_it fails on the old `pid:uuid` mint) and tests/unit/test_consumer_heartbeat.py (5 tests, of which 3 fail on the pre-fix consumer). test_the_lease_and_the_heartbeat_ask_one_machine_the_same_way pins the two to the single definition in `audit.host_id`, so a third copy cannot appear without the test noticing.
third_order.note: Proved rather than assumed: the tests were run against the pre-fix files and the failures recorded above. One of the lease tests does NOT fail pre-fix and its docstring says so, because a test that documents a rule is not the same thing as a test that would have caught the defect. process_alive is left open as task #21 with the fix written out: it needs `host` on every audit row plus four call sites, which is a schema change and not a same-turn edit. Splitting it is stated here rather than left implicit, so `after: 0` below counts the two sites this commit claims and no more.

grade.signature: a persisted pid with no host beside it, checked with os.kill (lease and heartbeat)
grade.note: Scoped to the two sites fixed. The third, process_alive, is task #21 and is NOT counted as fixed here.
